name: Chachapoyas Quechua
sweep_summary: The only works with stress in the title, Valqui & Chalco 2023 (Pontes, vol. 2, pp. 241-273; doi 10.29327/5382304.1-7), is squarely about Chachapoyas Quechua stress but could not be read: the DOI lands on a Pontes product page where the ebook is free but delivered only through a WooCommerce cart/checkout; OpenAlex marks it closed with no repository copy, archive. an open Brid 2024 review on SciELO Uruguay was also unreachable). The stress statement is nevertheless settled first-hand by the same author's open doctoral thesis (Valqui 2020, p. 152, held by the project): primary stress on the first syllable of the word with rhythmic right-to-left secondary stresses, no noun/verb split — which confirms the catalog's fixed: initial syllable coding and supersedes its current deciding source (Wikipedia paraphrasing Urban 2021, itself a second-hand line citing Taylor 1979). Valqui 2018 (Letras, p. 91) refines with a penult variant in some verbs and possible rhythmic secondary stress.

new_statements.quote: En el quechua de Chachapoyas, la prominencia acentual se asigna en la primera sílaba de la palabra con acentos secundarios que se construye de manera rítmica de derecha hacia izquierda por cada dos elementos métricos acentuables.
new_statements.translation: In Chachapoyas Quechua, accentual prominence is assigned to the first syllable of the word, with secondary stresses built rhythmically from right to left on every two stressable metrical elements.
new_statements.citation: Valqui Culqui, Jairo (2020). Patrones acentuales en el quechua de Chachapoyas y su implicancia para la reconstrucción del protoquechua. Tesis doctoral, Universidad Nacional Mayor de San Marcos, Lima. hdl 20.500.12672/11681 (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).
new_statements.locator: Conclusiones, conclusion 1, printed p. 152 (PDF page 173 of 209)
new_statements.reading: Fixed initial primary word stress for nouns and verbs alike (a single parameter setting: Left-Left-Left edge, iterative left-headed binary constituents, *(x( clash prevention), with rhythmic secondary stress. Confirms the catalog's fixed-dominant initial coding (initial stress) and refines it by adding rhythmic secondary stress; the same author's 2018 preliminary article (p. 91) also notes penult primary stress in some verb forms. Based on the author's own acoustic field data from Chachapoyas and Luya provinces.

(3) I downloaded Valqui 2018, Valqui 2020, Urban 2021 and Valqui et al. 2019 into (record). [...] Los parámetros del acento tanto para la Línea 0 como para la Línea 1 consignan el Margen Izquierdo a la Izquierda de la marca que se encuentra más a la Izquierda (I-I-I) y el parámetro de Construcción de Constituyentes Iterativos con el valor Izquierdo por cada par de secuencias acentuables.
sources.locator: Conclusiones, conclusion 1, printed p. 152 (PDF page 173); conclusion 2, p. 153
sources.note: Primary stress on the first syllable of the word, with rhythmic secondary stresses built right-to-left on every two stressable metrical elements; the same parameters cover nouns and verbs (no noun/verb split, unlike Santo Tomás's Quechua or Ferreñafe). Conclusion 2 (p. 153) adds that the initial-stress pattern plus rhythmic secondary stress is shared with southern Conchucos and Corongo Quechua, and is argued to be a Proto-Quechua retention. sources.quote: 'Interference from the original language of Chachapoyas may also be responsible for some drastic changes in Chachapoyas Quechua, such as shift of stress to the initial syllable and subsequent reduction of unstressed vowels (Taylor 1979).' This is the source behind the Wikipedia sentence our record quotes; it is a one-line second-hand mention, not a description.
sources.note: Second-hand summary (earlier in the paper attributed to Taylor 1979): initial stress, unusual within Quechuan, linked to unstressed-vowel reduction. This is the sentence Wikipedia paraphrases and the catalog carries; it confirms the classification but is not a first-hand phonological description.
